'''Mitio (Michio) Nagumo''' ({{langx|ja|南雲 道夫}}; May 7, 1905 &ndash; February 6, 1995) was a Japanese [[mathematician]], who specialized in the theory of [[differential equation]]s. He gave the first [[necessary and sufficient condition]] for [[Positive invariant set|positive invariance]] of [[closed set]]s under the flow induced by ordinary differential equations ([[Bony-Brezis theorem|Nagumo/Bony-Brezis theorem]]).<ref name=blanchini>{{citation|title=Survey paper: Set invariance in control|first=Franco|last= Blanchini|journal=Automatica |volume= 35 |number=11 |year= 1999|pages= 1747–1767| doi=10.1016/S0005-1098(99)00113-2}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Mitio Nagumo graduated from the Department of Mathematics at the [[Imperial University of Tokyo]] in March 1928. In March 1931 he was appointed Lecturer in the Faculty of Technology at the [[Kyushu University|Imperial University of Kyushu]]. In February 1932 he left [[Japan]] for an academic visit to [[University of Göttingen|Göttingen]], where he remained for two years. Upon his return from [[Göttingen]] in March 1934, he was appointed Lecturer in the Department of Mathematics at the [[Osaka University|Imperial University of Osaka]],<ref name=bio>{{citation|title=Mitio Nagumo|first=K|last= Yosida|
journal=Funkcialaj Ekvacioj|volume= 6 |year= 1966| url=http://fe.math.kobe-u.ac.jp/FE/Free/vol09/fe09-3.pdf}} {{in lang|eo}}</ref> and was promoted to Associate Professor in September that year, becoming Professor in the Faculty of Science in March 1936. In March 1937 Nagumo received a [[Doctor of Science]] degree from the [[Imperial University of Tokyo]]. In the 1960s he made a number of academic visits abroad, spending time at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] (where he visited [[Kurt Otto Friedrichs|Kurt Friedrichs]] and other old acquaintances from his time at [[University of Göttingen|Göttingen]]) and the [[Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul]] in 1960, followed by a visit to the [[National Tsing Hua University]] in 1963-64. He retired from [[Osaka University]] in December 1966, after which he was granted the title of Honorary Professor. He was subsequently appointed Professor at [[Sophia University]], from which he retired in March 1976, having reached [[mandatory retirement]] age.<ref name=collectedworks>{{cite book 
|last1= Yamaguti
|first1= Masaya
|last2= Nirenberg
|first2= Louis |author2-link=Louis Nirenberg
|last3= Mizohata 
|first3= Sigeru
|last4= Sibuya 
|first4=Yasutaka
|date= 1993
|title= Mitio Nagumo Collected Papers
|publisher= Springer Japan
|pages= 462–465
|isbn=978-4431549338}}</ref>

Much of Nagumo's original work was published in [[Japanese language|Japanese]] and [[German language|German]],<ref name=collectedworks/> however his research and teaching have influenced numerous mathematicians (especially in [[Japan]]) who have since made many of his results available in [[English language|English]].<ref name=hsieh-subiya>{{cite book 
|last1= Hsieh
|first1= Po-Fang
|last2=  Sibuya
|first2= Yasutaka
|date= June 1999
|title= Basic Theory of Ordinary Differential Equations 
|publisher= Springer
|isbn=9781461215066}}</ref>
